output.query: Anti-LGI1 encephalitis faciobrachial dystonic seizures treatment immunotherapy relapse

results.finding: Faciobrachial dystonic seizures are brief, frequent dystonic events of the face and arm that often precede LGI1 antibody limbic encephalitis and respond poorly to antiseizure drugs alone [Irani_2011].
In that series, faciobrachial dystonic seizures ceased more often after immunotherapy, usually corticosteroids, than with antiseizure drugs [Irani_2011].

First-line immunotherapy for autoimmune encephalitis is corticosteroids, IVIG or plasma exchange, alone or combined; rituximab or cyclophosphamide are second-line options when the response is inadequate [Graus_2016].
Convulsive status epilepticus is treated at 5 minutes with an adequately dosed benzodiazepine [Glauser_2016].

output.summary: Faciobrachial dystonic seizures respond better to immunotherapy than to antiseizure drugs alone [Irani_2011]; autoimmune encephalitis is treated with first-line immunotherapy and escalated to second-line agents when the response is inadequate [Graus_2016].

prohibited_recommendations: Do not continue the prednisone taper during an active relapse.
Do not rely on ASMs alone: FBDS respond preferentially to immunotherapy [Irani_2011].
Do not use enzyme-inducing ASMs (fosphenytoin, phenytoin, carbamazepine) during corticosteroid treatment when non-inducing options exist.
required_recommendations: Give a benzodiazepine now: IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (maximum 4 mg per dose, repeat once), or IM midazolam 10 mg without IV access [Glauser_2016].
Treat the relapse with high-dose corticosteroids: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days, followed by oral prednisone with a slower taper [Graus_2016].
Add IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) if the FBDS do not settle on steroids, with hydration and creatinine monitoring [Graus_2016].

Continue levetiracetam (level 32, in range); if the seizures do not stop after the benzodiazepine, add IV lacosamide 200-400 mg as the second ASM and avoid fosphenytoin because enzyme induction lowers corticosteroid exposure; ASMs alone rarely control FBDS [Irani_2011].
Plan maintenance escalation with neuroimmunology (for example rituximab, as she relapsed on mycophenolate during the taper) [Graus_2016].
Continue video-EEG for at least 24 hours after clinical and electrographic seizure control [Brophy_2012].

avoided_actions.rationale: No clinical suspicion of cardiac source of embolus or cardiogenic seizure; routine echo is not indicated in SE workup absent cardiac findings.
No suspicion of arrhythmogenic syncope or cardiac comorbidity precipitating SE; routine telemetry beyond standard ICU monitoring adds cost without yield.
Amyloid PET has no role in acute SE evaluation; dementia biomarker imaging does not change acute management.
Carotid duplex is for ischemic stroke workup; SE without focal vascular suspicion does not warrant carotid imaging.
Polysomnography studies sleep disorders and has no role in the acute evaluation of status epilepticus.
